correctness.rationale: The full weak constant equals the norm of S on L2(w) by the exact multiplication isometry. Osękowski's Theorem 1.2 gives the explicit lower bound e^{-2}/48 times sqrt(A log(1+A)) for arbitrarily large dyadic A2 characteristic A. Ivanisvili--Mozolyako--Volberg Theorem 4.1/4.6 gives the restricted characteristic-input upper bound C sqrt(A). Dividing proves the ratio lower bound, and choosing source thresholds tending to infinity gives an unbounded sequence.

value.rationale: The 2018 paper singled out characteristic-input restricted weak testing as a regime where the logarithmic correction disappears, but the full logarithm was not then known necessary. The 2026 sharpness theorem resolves that uncertainty. Their combination shows a genuine unbounded failure of restricted testing to capture the full weak norm and quantifies the minimum loss along some weights by a square-root logarithm, a natural structural boundary in weighted square-function theory.
